basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 8.' and it opens '(Vers. 8.) Et plantavit Dominus Deus paradisum in Eden, contra orientem. Pro paradiso, in'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 8.) Et plantavit Dominus Deus paradisum in Eden, contra orientem. Pro paradiso, in Hebraeo hortum habet: id est, GAN (גן). Porro EDEN (עדן), deliciae interpretantur. Pro quo Symmachus transtulit, paradisum florentem. Necnon quod sequitur, contra orientem, in Hebraeo MECEDEM (מקדם) scribitur, quod Aquila posuit ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς: et nos, ab exordio, possumus dicere. Symmachus vero, ἐκ πρώτης, et Theodotion, ἐν πρώτοις, quod et ipsum non orientem, sed principium significat. Ex quo manifestissime comprobatur, quod priusquam coelum et terram Deus faceret, paradisum ante condiderat, sicut et legitur in Hebraeo: Plantaverat autem Dominus Deus paradisum in Eden, a principio.
